_about: Budgets for .github/scripts/perf_budget.py: first-party bytes (uncompressed) and requests at load, per template and viewport, about 15% above the heaviest of four measurements on 2026-09-24. Raise one only for a change that is meant to cost more, and say why in the commit; the script's docstring has the procedure. JS raised 25 KB on every template on 2026-10-01: the shared script grew about 40 KB with the reading, search, listing, photo and collection fixes of that week (keyboard contents, citation previews, code copy, word-start search, load-failure notes, the photo lightbox, sharper images). The homepage desktop requests went from 54 to 63 on 2026-10-13: the Latest section fills its photography panel to the height of the tallest column, which loads three to five more thumbnails (measured 55). The literature page JS went from 595 to 605 KB the same day: the shelf's spines and the reading figures gained the calendar's hover card (measured 595.5 KB). The gallery JS went from 585 to 600 KB on 2026-10-14: gallery.js shows each photograph's edits as one tile, with the edits on hover and in the lightbox (measured 590.8 KB). The homepage desktop images went from 730 to 910 KB on 2026-10-18: the Latest section fills its photography column with the newest frames, so its weight follows the newest set, and the Ann Arbor set of that day (detailed graffiti and leaves at 400px, up to 64 KB a thumbnail) measured 797 KB. The prose post JS (blog/rating-systems.html) went from 545 to 555 KB on 2026-10-19: its six charts are now HTML bar charts whose hover cards load js/diagrams.js, the script a page fetches only when it has a diagram (measured 546.2 KB). CSS went from 290 to 296 KB on every template the same day: the one stylesheet gained the diagram layouts (bar charts, flow), the Save as PNG button and stacked tables for phones (measured 290.6 KB); the scripts behind them load only on pages that use them (js/diagrams.js). On 2026-10-22 the homepage desktop images went from 910 to 1,090 KB, and the blog listing images from 430 to 495 KB on a phone and 640 to 750 KB on a desktop: the photography strip under both pages loads ten frames drawn at random from the whole pool, so the image weight swings with the draw (four runs measured 873 to 928 KiB on the homepage desktop and 532 to 637 KiB on the blog desktop, with no change to either page between them; CI measured 431 KB on the blog phone), and the budget had no room for a heavy draw. On 2026-10-24 the CSS went from 296 to 305 KB on every template and the JS rose on every one (index and prose post 555 to 580 KB, blog 575 to 595, interactive post 575 to 600, literature 605 to 630, gallery 600 to 645): the commit before it already measured over (CSS 302.6 KB; JS 561.1, 576.0, 580.0, 609.5, 561.1 and 624.1 KB, after the gallery's place filters and the Halloween season), and the seasons added the season table and its loader to the shared script (about 10 KB) while their own styles moved out of the stylesheet into css/seasons/<key>.css, loaded only in season (measured CSS 302.6 KB; JS 570.9, 585.7, 590.5, 619.4, 570.8 and 634.2 KB). Later the same day the CSS went back from 305 to 300 KB: the rules every season shares moved out too, into css/season.css, loaded only while a season is on (measured 294.2 KB). On 2026-10-29 the JS rose 10 KB on every template (index and prose post 580 to 590 KB, blog 595 to 605, interactive post 600 to 610, literature 630 to 640, gallery 645 to 655): the shared script grew about 3 KB with the jargon tooltips' alias matching (a box label like "Apex / bare domain" underlines either half), memorial mode for a post in memory of someone (no season or birthday decorations on it) and Reddit embeds (drawn in the page's theme, as tall as the post says it is), and the budgets set on 2026-10-24 had no room left: CI measured 580.9, 595.8 and 580.8 KB on the index, blog and prose post, and the other templates, which load the same script, had little or none either. On 2026-11-06 the CSS went from 300 to 305 KB on every template and the literature page JS from 640 to 650 KB: the Reading Stats figures gained small pictures (bars for the stars, the years and the months, a scale against the Goodreads average, a shelf of spines, two rows) and four figures from a Goodreads export snapshot, data/reading-analysis.json, which bookshelf.js draws; the stylesheet had 0.1 KB of room before it (measured CSS 301.9 KB, literature JS 646.3 KB). On 2026-11-10 the CSS went from 305 to 313 KB on every template and the JS rose on every one (index and prose post 590 to 612 KB, blog 605 to 633, interactive post 610 to 639, literature 650 to 675, gallery 655 to 687): one round of work added the blog's list layout and Start here band, read marks and series progress, the shelf strip on book posts and authors in the command palette, replies from Bluesky under posts, a link to a run and full screen in the demo engine, the gallery's colour filter, exposure line and figures, the listening calendar, the Lab page and the rebuilt header menu (measured CSS 308.5 KB; JS 602.7, 623.6, 629.1, 664.9, 602.6 and 676.7 KB; the homepage's carousel and Explore tiles went the other way). The literature page's desktop images went from 150 to 290 KB and its requests from 38 to 43 the same day: the covers of the books in progress, the last two finished and the review cards are now files on this site, where they were Goodreads' and so not counted (measured 250.1 KB and 41 requests); the reader downloads no more than before.
